why: Applies the tidier `tanks.dev.progress.v1` mapping that the doc comment above DEVELOPER_KEY_PREFIX rejects, instead of prefixing the whole key. It is self-consistent -- read, write, remove and clear all agree on it -- so no single store's round trip breaks, and that self-consistency is exactly why it needs pinning: what it costs is the INVERSE, because names() strips only the prefix and hands back `progress.v1` where the store wrote `tanks.progress.v1`, and two store keys differing only by a leading `tanks.` would collapse onto one underlying key. 3 of 40 in storage.test.ts: the write-lands-under-the-prefix case, the scoped-enumeration case, and the injectivity/inverse case.
